project.name: SentrAI
project.description: SentrAI is an accountability-based security system for small organizations: it watches web, database and OS layers, turns anomalies into a 0-100 risk index, applies temporary reversible hotpatches when risk tolerance is crossed, and produces hash-chained evidence reports. The repo holds the project plan site (Jekyll) and a Python MVP (FastAPI core, Streamlit dashboard, Flask target lab, notifier). Note: this project has over 100 source files; consider scoping analysis to a subdirectory for faster results.

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Start with the README, which states SentrAI's core idea: small organizations already get alerts, but nobody acts on them in time and nobody can later prove who knew what and when. SentrAI watches the web, database and OS layers, turns anomalies into a 0-100 risk index, applies temporary reversible fixes when the organization's tolerance is crossed, and writes a tamper-evident evidence report. The full project plan expands this into the CIA+NA principles, per-layer data collection, the risk formula and the hotpatch workflow that the rest of the tour walks through in code.

tour.title: The MVP Contract
tour.description: The MVP is split into components (core, lab, dashboard, notifier) built against one shared interface contract. CONTRACT.md defines directory ownership and the Event JSON that collectors post to the core, so every later step speaks the same vocabulary of events, categories and incidents. The MVP README then explains how those pieces are run together on Windows, Linux or as systemd services.

tour.title: Launching the Demo
tour.description: run_demo.ps1 is the one-command entry for the demo: it builds per-component virtual environments, runs first-run configuration and API token setup, checks ports, then starts every component; run_demo.sh is its Bash twin for Linux/macOS. Both lean on cactai_config.py, the per-machine settings store and setup wizard that keeps environment settings in one JSON file. Understanding this launcher tells you which processes exist at runtime before you read any of them.
tour.languageLesson: PowerShell and Bash launchers often mirror each other. Keeping them as twins with the same flags (mode, demo speed, ports) lets one demo run cross-platform while each uses native process control (taskkill /T on Windows, process-group signals on Unix).

tour.title: Core API Entry Point
tour.description: main.py is the FastAPI application factory and the most depended-upon file in the graph: it defines the request models and every API endpoint for events, decisions, protection, reports and more. Its runtime Settings come from config.py, which reads environment variables and falls back to the setup wizard's saved values from Step 3. Everything the collector, dashboard and notifier do later is a call into these endpoints, as the core README describes.
tour.languageLesson: The app-factory pattern (a create_app function returning a FastAPI instance) lets tests build an isolated app with test settings, which is exactly what core/tests/conftest.py does with TestClient.

tour.title: Classifying Events, Scoring Risk
tour.description: Incoming events pass through a pluggable classifier chain: deterministic rules first, then the Jev AI classifier, then a keyword fallback, each labelling the event with a category and clipped confidence. jev_client.py wraps Jev with timeouts and a circuit breaker so an unavailable AI never stalls detection. risk.py turns those labels into the 0-100 risk index, including severity bands and the inaction penalty that makes ignored alerts get louder over time.
tour.languageLesson: A chain-of-responsibility classifier returns None when a stage cannot decide, letting the next stage try. Combined with a circuit breaker, it keeps an optional AI dependency from becoming a single point of failure.

tour.title: The Saguaro Orchestrator
tour.description: Saguaro is the warden at the heart of the core and the file with the widest reach: it owns incidents, the risk index from Step 5, notifications, the TTL hotpatch workflow and operator decisions. It works with deterministic specialist agents (Gatehouse, Vault, Watchtower, Garrison, Watchdog, Scribe and others) defined in agents.py. State is persisted in SQLite via state.py, and clock.py provides an advanceable demo clock so hours of inaction can be shown in minutes.

tour.title: Reversible Containment
tour.description: When risk crosses the organization's tolerance, Saguaro applies containment through the responder registry, which can both apply and revert actions; this is what lets every hotpatch expire unless a human makes it permanent. Blocks are enforced via the blocklist, and firewall.py optionally mirrors block_ip actions into nftables, iptables or netsh, in dry-run mode by default. This design reflects the project's never-hack-back ethic: it holds the line rather than attacking.

tour.title: Hash-Chained Evidence
tour.description: Accountability rests on audit.py, an append-only SHA-256 hash-chained log in SQLite whose triggers block UPDATE and DELETE, so tampering is detectable. reports.py builds Scribe's Security Evidence Report for an incident and renders it as JSON, Markdown and PDF, with pdfdoc.py providing a minimal standard-library PDF writer. Together they produce the proof of who knew what and when that Step 1 promised.
tour.languageLesson: A hash chain stores each entry's hash computed over its content plus the previous entry's hash. Changing any old record breaks every hash after it, so verification only needs to recompute the chain and compare the head hash.

tour.title: Optional AI Layer
tour.description: cactai_llm.py is a provider-agnostic LLM layer that picks Anthropic, OpenAI, DeepSeek or any OpenAI-compatible service from environment keys. Cyanide uses it as a drop-in replacement for Saguaro, asking a model for per-incident containment plans while invented actions are dropped. chat.py gives operators a read-only chat that inspects risk, incidents and the audit trail through tools, and ai.py reports which model is active and why it might be off.

tour.title: The Target Lab
tour.description: To demonstrate SentrAI, the lab provides Aegis Academy, a fictional Flask student portal that emits realistic web, DB and OS logs through logger.py and stores synthetic members in db.py. It enforces containment by refreshing its blocklist from the core's GET /blocklist every 2 seconds, closing the loop from Step 7. spines.py adds a tripwire deception layer: a honeypot login page, a planted honeytoken credential, bait rows and an IP tarpit.
tour.languageLesson: Flask's application-factory pattern (create_app) plus a __main__.py module lets the portal be launched with 'python -m target_app' and also built fresh inside each pytest test.

tour.title: Collector and Scout
tour.description: The collector is the bridge from logs to the core: it tails the target app's JSONL logs, approved nginx/sshd/journald server logs and a heartbeat, normalizes them into contract Events from Step 2 and sends them to the core, buffering while the core is down. parsers.py handles real server log formats using only the standard library. Scout is an AI-guided discovery tool that browses an unfamiliar system with read-only, root-confined tools and proposes log sources that a technician must approve, stored in sources.py.

tour.title: Attack Simulation
tour.description: scenario.py orchestrates the live demo story: a benign baseline, brute force, a pause, SQL injection and optional tripwires. Each attack script shares _common.py, whose safety guard refuses any non-localhost target. Running them against the lab portal from Step 10 drives events through the collector into the core, so you can watch risk rise until auto-blocking kicks in above 80.

tour.title: Dashboard and Notifier
tour.description: Operators interact through two surfaces that only talk to the core API. The Streamlit dashboard uses a thin CoreClient in api.py and pure, Streamlit-free helpers in shaping.py for risk bands and tables, which keeps its logic testable. The notifier polls the core for pending alerts and delivers them to Telegram or the console (with an email backup), using formatting.py for messages and inline buttons.

tour.title: Tests and Evaluation
tour.description: Confidence comes from layered tests: core fixtures in conftest.py build the FastAPI app for API tests, while test_e2e.py launches the real core, target app and collector as subprocesses and runs the lab attack scripts end to end. evaluate.py scores the classifier chain from Step 5 on a labelled event set with per-category precision. The GitHub Actions workflow runs the MVP pytest suites on both Ubuntu and Windows.
tour.languageLesson: GitHub Actions matrix builds run the same job across multiple operating systems. Testing on both Ubuntu and Windows matters here because the project ships PowerShell and Bash launchers and a firewall responder with OS-specific backends.

tour.title: Server Deployment
tour.description: Beyond the laptop demo, install.sh deploys SentrAI on a Linux server: it validates Python, creates the cactai service user and an /etc/cactai settings location, and installs the systemd units. cactai-core.service runs the uvicorn core with strict sandboxing, and cactai.target groups core, collector, dashboard and notifier so they start together. The deploy README explains the installer options and how to reach the dashboard over SSH.
tour.languageLesson: systemd targets group related units: each service is tied to the target and ordered After the core service, so startup order and lifecycle are managed declaratively instead of in a shell script.
